description:
DECISION: decompress_gunbatch() uses decoder.take((limit + 1) as u64) before read_to_end(), so the decompressor is capped at exactly limit+1 bytes streamed. If out.len() > limit after the read, it returns DecompressedTooLarge.

WHY RIGHT: The alternative — read_to_end() into an unbounded Vec, then check length — allocates the full decompressed output before the check is applied. Against a gzip bomb that expands to multiple GiB this would exhaust process memory (or trigger OOM kill) before the cap fires. The .take() wrapper delegates the cap to the I/O layer; the allocator never sees more than limit+1 bytes. The +1 is intentional: it lets the code distinguish 'exactly at limit' (ok) from 'exceeded limit' (error) with a single read.

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED:
- Chunked read with manual accumulator: more code, same semantic, no benefit.
- Checking compressed size as a proxy: gzip compression ratios are unbounded; a 1 KB input can expand to GiB.
- Using a hard ulimit on the process: not portable and would crash the process rather than return a typed error.
title: Gzip bomb cap via .take(limit+1), not allocate-then-check
